messages:
Alex R: Heads-up — the new onboarding sample app is hitting weirdly different error shapes across SDKs. iOS gives a vague string, node returns structured JSON with status, and the python SDK just raises a generic Exception. This blew up the demo today (401 vs auth_error). Anyone seen this?

Maya Chen: Yup, saw that in the test matrix. Looks like we never fully aligned the error envelope across SDKs after the auth-backoff changes. We need: typed exceptions + clear retry hint + consistent top-level fields (code, message, status, retry_after?).

Jon Park: iOS currently maps HTTP 401/403 to AuthError but it doesn't include a retry hint or a help_url. The sample app expected `RetryableError` for 429 only and tried to backoff, but the SDK threw and the UI crashed.

Priya Singh: Sample app reported stack: `UnhandledPromiseRejection: Error: auth failure` — that's the node wrapper, it lost the structured metadata. I can update the sample to read `error.status` and fall back to text, but we should fix SDK parity not just sample.

Maya Chen: Proposal: standard envelope keys = code (string), status (int), message (string), retryable (bool), retry_after (int seconds, optional), help_url (string, optional). And typed exceptions mapped from code, e.g. `AuthError`, `RateLimitError`, `TransientError`, `ValidationError`.

Alex R: Sounds reasonable. Can we add a small JSON example to the spec so SDKs can copy/paste?

Maya Chen: Sure — example envelope: 

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "rate_limit_exceeded",
    "status": 429,
    "message": "Too many requests",
    "retryable": true,
    "retry_after": 30,
    "help_url": "https://docs.redwood.ai/errors#rate_limit_exceeded"
  }
}
```

Maya Chen: Notes: 5xx -> TransientError (retryable=true), 429 -> RateLimitError (retryable=true + retry_after when available), 401/403 -> AuthError (retryable=false unless docs specify token refresh flow).

Jon Park: What about status code mapping when gateway returns non-standard status (e.g., 499 or custom 430)? We should fallback to `TransientError` for unknown 4xx with `retryable=false` unless body has `retryable=true`.

Priya Singh: I can add a tiny integration test in the sample app that asserts the SDK returns a typed exception with `.retryable` and `.status`. That will catch regressions. Will also add a UI-friendly message when `help_url` exists.

Alex R: Ownership & timeline? I propose: Priya — sample app tests + UI update (ETA 3 days). Jon — iOS & node SDK parity patches (ETA 5 days). Maya — update errors spec doc and add a changelog entry (ETA 2 days). I'll coordinate release notes and break this into three PRs.

DevEx Bot: Reminder: new `errors` spec PR created template: /templates/error-spec.md — please link it in PR description.

Maya Chen: Also thinking telemetry: add `error.code` tag in SDK logs so we can alert on spikes for specific codes (e.g., auth_error burst after a rollout). Also expose a sample failing prompt in the repo that reproduces the bad path.

Jon Park: Agree on telemetry. One more thing — ensure `auth` failures that are transient (e.g. temporary token service outage) can opt-in to `retryable=true` with an enum reason `auth_temporary`. Otherwise OAuth 401 should stay non-retryable.

Priya Singh: I will send a PR with tests + sample changes today and link it here. Assigning reviewers: @Jon Park pls check iOS mapping, @Maya Chen pls verify spec.

Alex R: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll also add a small migration note in the SDK changelogs about the new `retry_after` field. :thumbsup:
